summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 5 in Preterit-wa (Bilgic Der Beruf eines Kesselverzinkers/6)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr mayo hedi ṭrewolan maq qəryawoṯo, ʕudinawo bi dəkano.
data.translation: Später ließen wir von den Dörfern ab und wir arbeiteten (nur) im Geschäft.

rationale: First Preterit-wa box; ṭre- plus agent -lan and -wo supports this box independently of the retrospective translation.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/83)

data.turoyo: Bayto lo+ṭrewalle.
data.translation: They didn’t spare a house.
data.ref: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/83

rationale: First sense-2 example in new Preterit-wa box; exhaustive negation with a house parallels existing leave-no-doctor use.

evidence.cite: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/83

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Talay 2/25)

data.turoyo: mi naqqa d qṭil u mafaryono w d mamṭe l Bsorino, kətwa šəbbak, čučəko wa hawxa, ṭrewalle bu qawra..., bu qabrayḏe
data.translation: Seit der Zeit als der Maphrian ermordet und (sein Leichnam) nach Bsorino gebracht wurde, gab es eine Öffnung (lit.: Fenster), sie war so klein, die man in seinem Grab zurückgelassen hatte.

rationale: Thin Preterit-wa I.2 cell, previously one example; leaving an opening in a tomb, source self-repair qawra.../qabrayḏe retained.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 3 in Infinitiv (Jan 2.4/966)

data.turoyo: Mədone naʕime, ṭroyo d lebo naʕimo, lo, lo... lo, lo.
data.translation: Small matters, a little hurting of the heart, no, no... no, no.

rationale: First Infinitiv box, I.3 with d lebo; nominal phrase is preserved without inventing a finite subject. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.10/2685)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Abuna, bat 68 mšane, mən taṯir ṭrewole aʕlox?
data.translation: Jan: Abuna, he passed away in sixty-eight; what effect had it left on you?

rationale: Preterit-wa I.2 remains thin after round 1 and gives another box for the taṯir phrase. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Jan 4.I/323)

data.turoyo: Alyas ʕAnṭar: Əno haka kaṯowo, ṭrewayli ‘Ḥuyoḏo’. Əəəə ḥzeli kit faraġ gabi. Qayəm umarno gədʕəwadno ʕwodo ʕadi.
data.translation: Alyas Antar: I, as a writer, left Huyodo. Uh, I saw that I had some spare time. I get up and say: I will do ordinary work.

rationale: Thin Preterit-wa I.2 cell; exact ṭrewayli spelling retained, with editorial segmentation left open. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: New sense 1b: (mit l-) j-m etwas durchgehen lassen, j-n ungeschoren davonkommen lassen

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: (mit l-) j-m etwas durchgehen lassen, j-n ungeschoren davonkommen lassen

rationale: A personal l-suffix and offence demonstrative, without a permitted-action clause, express threatened retaliation. Two tokens at JL 15.6/8 and the independent JTM 1.6/7 context support one constructional subsense, not separate forgiveness and sparing senses.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/110

summary: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/46)

data.turoyo: Šqal di ṣənʕa w ṭray du mal. U mal kəzzeyo, i ṣənʕa lə kəzzayo.
data.translation: nimm denjenigen mit einer Ausbildung und laß denjenigen, der Besitz hat. Der Besitz geht zu Ende, die Ausbildung hat aber kein Ende.
data.ref: Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/46

rationale: Thin Imperativ sense-2 cell; independently interpretable contrast between trained and wealthy men.

evidence.cite: Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/46

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (Hors 1/32)

data.turoyo: W ḥatta ṭorənwaylan saʕaye w tre saʕayat, ono b šaxṣi ṭrallalli, hul arbʕo saʕayat <...>
data.translation: Sie ließen uns ein, zwei Stunden lang (warten); mich persönlich ließen sie einmal vier Stunden lang (warten) <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa sense-2 cell; duration complement, with waiting explicitly editorial/inferred.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Hors 1/32)

data.turoyo: W ḥatta ṭorənwaylan saʕaye w tre saʕayat, ono b šaxṣi ṭrallalli, hul arbʕo saʕayat <...>
data.translation: Sie ließen uns ein, zwei Stunden lang (warten); mich persönlich ließen sie einmal vier Stunden lang (warten) <...>

rationale: Unusual ṭrallal-li Preterit lateral sequence; paired with habitual form in the same short context, segmentation left open.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Hors 2/18)

data.turoyo: Ṭrayli ono, ʕobanno gabe, nošo ṭro lo ʕobər.
data.translation: Laß mich einmal zu ihm gehen. Niemand sonst soll hereinkommen.

rationale: Female addressee with first-person permittee -li, contrasted with unsuffixed ṭro in a negated dependent clause. Added for the construction contrast, not an inherited thin-cell count.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (JL 11.11/9)

data.turoyo: W moliwayna ḥlime, ḥeḏər ṣiṭo, aṭ=ṭarfe taxawat hawxa ʕal ḥḏoḏe, maḥtiwaynanne ʕal u=bayto, lo ṭoriwayna mede ftiḥo bayn aṭ=ṭarfani, d u=ʕafro lo=noḥət laltaḥ.
data.translation: Wir füllten die Zweige dick auf, etwa eine Spanne hoch, in Schichten übereinander; wir legten sie auf das Haus und ließen keine offene Stelle zwischen diesen Zweigen, damit die Erde nicht herunterrieseln konnte.

rationale: Fills the remaining Infectum-wa sense-2 slot to five; explicit object mede plus ftiḥo and purpose clause explain construction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JL 14.8/11)

data.turoyo: Tamo ap=poliṣ əšmo mʕawannalli. Lo=tralle ʕəbri li=qaraqole. Me tamo daʕiri am=morayḏa lu=bayto.
data.translation: Da halfen mir die Polizisten ein wenig, sie ließen sie nicht in die Polizeistation hinein. Daraufhin kehrten die Angehörigen (des Mädchens) nach Hause zurück.

rationale: Thin Preterit sense-1 cell; bare dependent ʕəbri with police as matrix subject. Preserve plain-t source spelling.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (JL 15.6/8)

data.turoyo: lə=gṭorinalux yo, bəṯr me d momeluxlan, lə=gṭorinalux haṯe <...>
data.translation: Das lassen wir dir nicht durchgehen. Nachdem du uns hast schwören lassen, lassen wir dir das nicht durchgehen. <...>

rationale: First example of new constructional subsense 1b; two tokens, including overt offence demonstrative haṯe, kept in one quotation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JL 16.7/21)

data.turoyo: E pa lo=ṭorənwa, maṣərre w maṣərre feme w lo=tralle,
data.translation: Aber sie ließen ihn ja nicht (antworteten), sie hatten ihn gefesselt· und ihm den Mund zugebunden, und sie ließen ihn nicht.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.1: permission denied with an omitted answer complement; paired Preterit retained inside quotation, without a second duplicate listing.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (JL 20.7/45)

data.turoyo: W ḥṣəlle, w ṭəryole hawxa, w u=admo konoḥət.
data.translation: Er drückte und hielt den Daumen so, und das Blut floß herab.

rationale: Unusual Preterit ṭəryole contrasts with ordinary ṭrele; short posture context, with no new physical-holding sense.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (JTM 1.5/47)

data.turoyo: "E", — məlle, — "məs samno, stad, i ʕašərto, u el hawxa ṭləble, lə ṭreli lebayye."
data.translation: Er antwortete: Was soll ich denn machen, Meister? Der Stamm, meine Leute haben es sich nun einmal so gewünscht, und ich wollte sie nicht enttäuschen.

rationale: Thin Preterit I.3; negated lebo construction motivating acquiescence, rather than a new disappoint sense.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (JTM 1.6/7)

data.turoyo: d oṯe mənayye, lə kṭurallanyo, məd koṯe mənayye, ṭər saymi, lə kubinala.
data.translation: Wenn sie imstande wären, würden sie uns das nicht durchgehen lassen. Sollen sie tun, was sie können, wir geben sie nicht heraus.

rationale: Independent source for new subsense 1b; personal suffix without an overt allowed-action clause in an explicit hostility context.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (JTM 3.2/4)

data.turoyo: Kətwo zlam mamur, ʕal u mal du mamurawo, am məḏyoye w a ʕəwardnoye ṭralle lebe d ḥḏoḏe daʕiri.
data.translation: Es gab da einen Beamten, wegen des Besitzes dieses Beamten stritten sich die Leute aus ʿIwardo und Midyat. (Die Leute von ʿIwardo) kehrten zurück.

rationale: Thin Preterit I.3 cell; reciprocal lebe d ḥḏoḏe, with edition’s dispute translation retained.

summary: example for sense 6 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.2/8)

data.turoyo: Mənayye ġalabe aṯən saymiwo qontrol d ḥozən, kit baynoṯayye saġ aw lo, ḥuzanwunne ka šəkəl miṯe, məftakriwo d miṯe ne w ṭuranwunne.
data.translation: Viele (Muslime) kamen und kontrollierten, um festzustellen, ob unter ihnen noch Lebende waren oder nicht. Sie kamen ihnen wie Tote vor, sie dachten, sie seien tot und ließen von ihnen ab.

rationale: First Infectum-wa example for clarified I.6; apparent corpses are left alone after inspection.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.3/8)

data.turoyo: W b Anḥəl stene nafəl kewo bənne, w aṭ ṭaye məḥanwo bənne, lə ṭuranwo d nəfqi <...>
data.translation: Auch in Anḥil erkrankten sie, und die Muslime schossen auf sie und ließen sie nicht (das Dorf) verlassen. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.1: explicit d-clause, contrasting with the preceding elliptical permission example.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (JTM 3.3/9)

data.turoyo: U dayroyo ṭər məǧġəl aʕmayxu.
data.translation: Der Mönch soll mit euch sprechen.

rationale: Short ṭər form before a third-person Infectum, not a new sense; whole simple sentence.

summary: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (JTM 5.2/65)

data.turoyo: e fət hat w ṭray i səsto harke!
data.translation: Nun, dann setze du über und lass das Pferd hier.

rationale: Thin Imperativ I.2 cell; direct-object mare and explicit location, contrasting with permission clauses.

summary: example for sense 6 in Imperativ (JTM 5.2/78)

data.turoyo: daxil diḏux, ṭrayli.
data.translation: Ich bitte dich inständig, lass mich.

rationale: First direct-suffix Imperativ example for clarified I.6; plea for non-interference.

summary: example for sense 5 in Preterit (JTM 5.3/18)

data.turoyo: komər ʕabər li ḥḏo mənayye, ḥəlle i kačke latyo šafərto, ṭrele mena. komər ʕabər li ḥreto steṭ ṭrele mena <...>
data.translation: Er betrat eines davon, sah, dass das Mädchen nicht schön war, und ließ es in Ruhe. Er betrat auch das andere Zimmer und ließ es in Ruhe. <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit I.5; two repeated men-targets in one short example, counted once as an example.

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum (Lahdo martyrdom/16)

data.turoyo: Ono ṭoreno mə Mšiḥo? Ono ono bak kayono koṭoreno mə Mšiḥo.
data.translation: I leave Jesus? I will not, no matter what, leave Jesus.

rationale: Thin Infectum I.5; religious allegiance participant, with rhetorical denial and no inserted Turoyo negator.

summary: example for sense 5 in Preterit (Lahdo martyrdom/28)

data.turoyo: At tane komər ṭralle mi ʕaskaraṯṯe, mi emo w mu babaṯṯe, aq qadišani du ṭurano d Ṭur ʕAbdin w aṯən ʕbədde hol d maxlaṣṣe ruḥayye.
data.translation: Thus these saints of the Ṭūr ʿAbdīn mountains left their armies, their parents and came to worship (God) until they reached salvation.

rationale: Brings Preterit I.5 to five examples; coordinated men-complements of army and parents support giving up association.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (MAC MuA Quzko/12)

data.turoyo: U+šaqṣ d̥ṭore lebe dəḥḏoḏe, lazəm lo+məġbən
data.translation: The person who offends one another, he mustn’t get angered

rationale: Thin Infectum I.3; generic reciprocal lebo frame, edition wording retained.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/94)

data.turoyo: Towənwa ṭawwe, lo+kṭorənwa, áydarbo kṭorən yani?
data.translation: Had they been good, they would not have allowed it, how would they allow it, like?
data.ref: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/94

rationale: Fills Infectum-wa I.1 to five; counterfactual permission, distinct from habitual denied permission.

evidence.cite: MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/94

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Interview 2/49)

data.turoyo: N. Mḥásyene. Miḥasən am+miṯayḏux, ŭ Aloho ṭore dəṯxu, tavda.
data.translation: They are blessed. May your dead be blessed, and may God spare (lit. ‘abandon’) you, together (with mine).

rationale: Makes the preservation extension in clarified I.1 explicit with the edition’s spare wording, not an invented forgiveness translation.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (MAC NE Mem and Zin/20)

data.turoyo: Omar, ‘Mămo, lawo, qayyo? Lhǝn mḥélelux?’ ‘Lo.’ ‘Ṭrele lebux?’ ‘Lo.’ ‘Mqatalle aʕmux?’ ‘Lo.’ ‘E qay bemaʕd hat?’
data.translation: He says, ‘Mămo, my boy, what’s up? Has someone beaten you?’ ‘No.’ ‘Offended you?’ ‘No.’ ‘Fought with you?’ ‘No.’ ‘So why are you listless?’

rationale: Thin Preterit I.3; clear brief question with possessed heart object.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (MAC NE Mother Mary saves Sultan’s son/9)

data.turoyo: E, rḥímowa. Lə+ṭralle lebe. Lə+ṭralle lebe, laṯi. Áydarbo g̊d̥owe?
data.translation: Yes, he was beloved. They didn’t upset him (lit. ‘they didn’t leave his heart’). They didn’t upset him, (but) he didn’t come back. What happens next (lit. ‘how will it be’)?
data.ref: MAC NE Mother Mary saves Sultan’s son/9

rationale: Completes Preterit I.3 cell to five; negated plural agents and personal lebo object.

evidence.cite: MAC NE Mother Mary saves Sultan’s son/9

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum (MAC NE Sterka Zera/7)

data.turoyo: Əmmo, ‘Lo-kṭorutu mini?’ Əmmi, ‘Lo, áydarbo kṭorina minax?!’
data.translation: She said, ‘Aren’t you going to leave me?’ They said, ‘No, how could we leave you?!’

rationale: Thin Infectum I.5; negative question and rhetorical response with explicit men-person complements.

summary: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (PrS 6/8)

data.turoyo: Mamṭəyola d futḥila. Səmme w lo səmme, lo ftiḥo. Omər: “Ṭrawulla tamhone hol ṣafro d suyamno qliḏo li ʕulbo.” Maḥtulle w ṭrayulle.
data.translation: Sie holte sie, um sie zu öffnen; aber wie sie es auch anfingen, die Schachtel liess sich nicht öffnen. Da sagte er: »Lass die Schachtel dort stehen bis morgen; dann will ich einen Schlüssel für sie machen lassen«. Sie setzten sie hin und liessen sie stehen;

rationale: Completes Imperativ I.2 to five; plural command and feminine object suffix, with box referent supplied in context.

summary: example for sense 6 in Imperativ (PrS 15/28)

data.turoyo: U šulṭono omər: “Qumu mibezu aʕ ʕasekir, ṭrawulle. Qoṭəl w kəmšaləḥ, nošo lo kəmtane.”
data.translation: Darauf befal der Sultan den Soldaten, sich zu zerstreuen und ihn zu verlassen: wenn er Leute ausraube und tödte, solle Niemand etwas dazu sagen.

rationale: Thin Imperativ I.6; no-interference continuation makes leave-alone interpretation explicit.

summary: example for sense 6 in Imperativ (PrS 20/7)

data.turoyo: U bazərgan maḥəṣle, omər: “Koyo u səsyo?” Əmmi: “Lo kmibayən.” Omər: “Ḥzawu u kurəko bi dukṯo yo?” Azzən, lo ḥzalle. Omər: “Luwe mawbele.” Omər: “Ṭrawulle.”
data.translation: Der Kaufmann erwachte und fragte: »Wo ist mein Pferd?« »Es ist verschwunden« erhielt er zur Antwort. »So seht zu, ob der Junge noch an seinem Platze ist«. Die Diener gingen hin und fanden ihn nicht. »Er hat's weggenommen« sagte der Kaufmann, »aber lasst ihn nur«.

rationale: Thin Imperativ I.6; independently interpretable disappearance context, direct suffixed boy object.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 27/49)

data.turoyo: Zahar omər: “Ṭrawyo i ḥoṯo ləno w i aṯto luxat.” Məlle l Dewe Raš, omər: “Ṭrowe.”
data.translation: da sagte Sâhär zum schwarzen Wolf: »Seine Schwester möge mir, seine Frau aber dir zu Teil werden«. »So möge es sein«, antwortete dieser.

rationale: Unusual fused feminine Ṭrawyo beside masculine assent Ṭrowe; modal I.1, preserving source form.

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum (PrS 34/45)

data.turoyo: Ap pəsmam du qašo qṭəlle u qašo, fləġġe u baytayḏe ʕar ruḥayye. Ṭərena mu qašo.
data.translation: Nun tödteten die Vettern des Pfaffen diesen und teilten sein Eigentum unter sich. –. Lassen wir den Pfaffen und kehren wir zu Nûre zurück.

rationale: Thin Infectum I.5: men-marked discourse topic, an extension rather than a second narrative-management sense.

summary: example for sense 6 in Imperativ (PrS 34/86)

data.turoyo: Laxwa ṭrayye, lə quṭlatle, u greʕayḏan yo.
data.translation: aber lass ihn und tödte ihn nicht, denn er ist unser Diener

rationale: Thin Imperativ I.6; direct suffix -ye and explicit refusal of killing establish leave-alone construction.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (PrS 59/70)

data.turoyo: Kətwole barṯo kayəsto lu malko, lə qṭəlole l Zaydin, ṭrelelayo.
data.translation: Der König hatte aber eine schöne Tochter, die tötete Seidin nicht, sondern liess sie für sich am Leben.

rationale: Unusual dense Preterit suffix sequence ṭrelelayo, with a feminine patient kept alive; no normalisation of segmentation.

summary: example for sense 6 in Preterit (PrS 70/31)

data.turoyo: mḥalaqlile i ʕezo, daʕər u ruʕyo w ṭrelelan.
data.translation: da habe ich ihm die Ziege hingeworfen, und er kehrte um und liess uns in Ruhe.

rationale: First Preterit example for clarified I.6; direct suffix and cessation of pursuit.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (4/20)

data.turoyo: W bi dukṯo, d kfayti bam maye, kṭorən bəṯrayye šop rabo w ḥəworo, xd i kaffe.
data.translation: Und da, wo sie durchfahren, lassen sie eine große, weiße Spur hinter sich, wie schaum.

rationale: Inanimate ships leave a wake: distinct cause/trace participants, making this more informative than the existing human-agent contexts.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (11/42)

data.turoyo: Uʕdo harke ṭurena Murde, faytina l Məḏyaḏ w aq qəryawoṯayḏa!
data.translation: Hier wollen wir Mardin verlassen und zu Midyat und seinen Dörfern übergehen!

rationale: Short direct topic object plus faytina l-: explicit narrative transition absent from the existing physical-retention examples.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (25/65)

data.turoyo: Ḥa komər lu ḥreno, komər: "Yabo, ono fləġli ak kallatani kulle ʕam am miṯe. Kul miṯo, qayəṯle ʕaṣro kallat. Hat gdubenux i ḥəṣṣayḏux, ṭruyo ʕabbasiye!"
data.translation: Einer spricht zum anderen: "Mensch! Ich habe doch das ganze Geld unter die toten verteilt. Auf jeden toten kommen zehn Para. Ich gebe dir deinen Anteil, er soll eine 'abbasiye sein."

rationale: Unusual fused ṭruyo in a clear coin-allocation clause; exact hwy segmentation remains open.

summary: example for sense 6 in Imperativ (43/37)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Ya aḥuni, zux b darbux w ṭrili b ḥal diḏi!"
data.translation: Er sprach: "Freund! Geh deines Weges und laß mich in Ruhe!"

rationale: Completes Imperativ I.6 to five; direct person suffix plus explicit b ḥal diḏi.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (61/375)

data.turoyo: W ṭrowutu saġ šani, w i ḥəkeyayḏan tayimo.
data.translation: und ihr bleibt mir lange Leben, und unsere Geschichte ist zu ende.

rationale: Unusual fused ṭr-owutu closing blessing; audience reply absent from source is excluded.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (62/191)

data.turoyo: Gdobina fəlge lawo w fəlge lawo, ṭrəxlile, a tre gmayṯi
data.translation: Wir wollen die eine Hälfte davon dem einen und die andere Hälfte dem anderen geben; sie sollen sie essen und werden dann sterben.

rationale: Unusual fused plural eating complement, contrasting with feminine-eater /196.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (62/196)

data.turoyo: Kal komamṭelilxu ḥabušo, mədlux fəlge hat axul, w fəlge emi ste ṭrəxlole!”
data.translation: Seht, ich habe euch hier einen Apfel gebracht; nimm du die eine Hälfte davon und laß meine Mutter die andere Hälfte essen!"

rationale: Unusual fused ṭr+əxlole with an overt mother as eater; preferable to longer /167.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (64/89)

data.turoyo: faqaṭ i saġitiye ṭaw mu mawto yo, ṭro loweno u abro du šulṭono, ṭroweno baqoro!
data.translation: Leben ist aber besser als Tod; laß mich nicht Sohn des Sultans, sondern meinetwegen Rinderhirt sein!

rationale: Unusual fused first-person hwy component; complete contrasting negative/positive proposition.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (75/109)

data.turoyo: Komər: “Lo zayʕət! Adlalyo gṭoreno ḥozət.”
data.translation: «Hab keine Angst! Heute Abend werde ich dich wiedersehend machen.»

rationale: Short sight-enabling ḥozət complement documents causative force of lassen; no separate make-see sense.

summary: example for sense 5 in Imperativ (88/241)

data.turoyo: U=faqqa omər: “O, i=čirokaṯe latyo basəmto! Ṭrawu m i=čirokaṯe! Ono gdomanno ḥḏo!”
data.translation: Jetzt sprach der Schulmeister: "Oh! Diese Geschichte ist nichtschön! Laßt diese Geschichte! Ich werde eine erzählen!"

rationale: Seven modal examples have moved out of I.5, leaving three genuine men-target Imperativ examples. This explicit stop-this-story command supplies the fourth.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (95/262)

data.turoyo: Ṭrowat xaṭər di ǧwanmeriye, d səmlux.
data.translation: So sollst du der edlen tat zu liebe, die du getan hast, am Leben bleiben!

rationale: Unusual fused second-person singular hwy owat after permissive ṭr-, contrasting with earlier third-person/first-person/plural forms.

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum-wa (107/147)

data.turoyo: E, baʕ mə gsaymono, mə gdəmmalax? Uʕdo, d ṭorewa meni, d əṯyowayno, nəǧlowayno l ṣaʕrax w d mamiṯowaynolax bab barčitat, i naqlayo gzəbṭatwa ʕaqəl diḏax, naqqa ḥreto noše zede hawxa, d l əmmatwa.”
data.translation: Was soll ich tun, was soll ich dir sagen? Wenn er mir doch jetzt freie Hand ließe, daß ich käme und dir die Haare ausrisse und dich mit Rohrstöcken zu Tode prügelte! Dann würdest du wohl zu Verstand kommen und nicht wieder anderen Leuten so etwas sagen! -

rationale: First Infectum-wa I.5 example; explicit meni plus unreal wish for free action, distinct from ordinary modal permission.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (112/173)

data.turoyo: Way aʕli, aydarbo u ṭaršano, w aṯməl l Ṭafšo maməṯle b ruḥe w ṭrelelelan dlo ḥšəmto!
data.translation: Zum Kuckuck! All dieses Vieh, und gestern hat Tafscho getan, als ob er sterben müßte, und hat uns ohne Abendessen gelassen!

rationale: Unusual expanded Preterit -le-le-lan with a clear privative state; preserve the full source suffix sequence.

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum-wa (113/190)

data.turoyo: Haka d ḥozatwa u abrayḏi u abro du šah du ʕaǧam, gədṭoratwa me Mḥammad w darḥal gdoṯatwa bəṯre!
data.translation: Wenn du meinen Sohn, den Sohn des Schahs von Persien sähest, würdest du sofort Muhammed fahren lassen und jenem nachlaufen.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.5, counterfactual second-person feminine and explicit me-person; no new romance-specific sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 1.2/34)

data.turoyo: W bi muʕawanayḏe ṭrele d mḥayṣəl bi mənṭəqa bar rayat da mšiḥoye.
data.translation: And with his help, he enabled the party to obtain votes from the Christians in the region.

rationale: Fills the fifth Preterit I.1 slot after the round-1 police example; d-clause and instrumental help are explicit, though the party referent is supplied by discourse. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Jan 1.16/652)

data.turoyo: Binayat ġalabe šafire maʕmarre w ṭranne dlo more w aṯən.
data.translation: They built very beautiful buildings, and left them without owners and came away.

rationale: Retains the contracted written ṭranne and an explicit ownerless resulting state; morphology is not silently expanded. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Jan 3.46/1268)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Man ṭər soyəm u medano, abuna, man?
data.translation: Jan: Who is to do this thing, Father, who?

rationale: Interrogative man plus reduced ṭər and soyəm illustrates modal scope in a question, beyond the earlier declarative/exhortative contexts. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Jan 4.I/231)

data.turoyo: Ṭrowe ṣənʕa, ṭrowe froso, ṭrowe rahṭo, yaʕni mən ṣənʕa d kətyo ṭruyo.
data.translation: Be it a craft, be it publishing, be it business, that is, whatever craft it is, let it be.

rationale: One example for the disjunctive enumeration, with final feminine ṭruyo; not four additions for repeated words. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: Restore ṣ in ʕaṣriye
rationale: The cited verse 24/279 reads 'kul ʕaṣriye'. The entry loses the emphatic consonant ṣ; this is not clitic, accent or vowel-length normalization.

summary: Translate kallawat as 'money'
rationale: The Turoyo says 'kallawat k-oba-lle', and 77/194 translates this as 'Sie gab ihnen soviel Geld, wie sie wollten.' 'Gold' introduces a material not specified by either the cited Turoyo or its translation. Other supplied glossary examples likewise translate kallawat as money (e.g. ʕmr 2, III).

summary: Restore ṣ in b-ṣulḥ
rationale: 29/298 reads 'b ṣulḥ w ənsaniye'. The entry substitutes s for ṣ in the word for peace; the supplied glossary also has ṣulḥ in ʔzl and sym. Keep the entry's clitic boundary and surrounding wording.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: lassen (mod); in Segenswünschen auch: behüten, bewahren
rationale: Positive blessings with Aloho and a personal suffix or nominal object are already represented by LB 259; MAC NE Interview 2/49 explicitly supports preservation, beyond bare permission.

summary: Sense 6: revise the gloss
after: to leave someone/something alone, in peace
rationale: Direct-object non-interference is distinct from men-governed sense 5. Result-state clauses are already covered by sense 2 (11/66, 24/279, 11/266); the hungry example belongs there rather than defining a second state-result sense.

summary: New idiom: ṭrowe rišayxu basimo 'Wunschformel: mögt ihr gesund/vergnügt bleiben; auch als Kondolenz'

data.headword: ṭrowe rišayxu basimo 'Wunschformel: mögt ihr gesund/vergnügt bleiben; auch als Kondolenz'
data.turoyo: Kəmmənne "ṭrowe rišayxu basimo", yaʕni kəmsalən more du miṯo.
data.translation: Sie sagen zu ihnen: Mögt ihr gesund bleiben, d.h. sie trösten die Angehörigen des Toten.

rationale: Explicitly identified as condolence in the Turoyo; rišayxu search finds the related ḥyy formula but no matching ṭry phrase. Single attested context. Broadened in batch 2: 63/348 uses the phrase in a closing wish, so condolence is one function, not its lexical definition.

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore raḥa (mit l-) 'j-m Ruhe lassen'

data.turoyo: Məd hawiwo u waxtawo, ann ahali yaʕni an noše, d əzzewolən u ḥəss, əzzənwo, ummiwo, bu qaraqol, lə kṭurallan raḥa, mu ḥəss.
data.translation: Wenn diese Zeit gekommen war, dann gingen die Anwohner, d.h. die Leute, die vom Lärm betroffen waren, zur Polizei und sagten: Sie lassen uns wegen des Lärms keine Ruhe.

rationale: Abstract peace object plus affected l-suffix; no matching ṭry collocation in raḥa lookup. Keep under Idiomatic phrases, not a new numbered sense.

summary: New idiom: ṭrowelux haž me ruḥux 'achte auf dich selbst'

data.headword: ṭrowelux haž me ruḥux 'achte auf dich selbst'
data.turoyo: N. Qām mərre lu+Šamʕən du+Išḳo, ǝmmi, ‘Ḳurro, ṭrowelux h͜āž me ruḥux, gədquṭlilux ha, ṭrowelux hāž me ruḥux’.
data.translation: They up and said to Šamʕən Išḳo, they say ‘Boy, take care of yourself, they will kill you, yes, take care of yourself’.
data.ref: MAC Murder in Kfarze, Interview with Numan/47

rationale: Whole ṭro+owe-lux haž me ruḥux phrase, with the concern noun in the hwy clause; haž lookup has no matching idiom. Single source, repeated warning.

evidence.cite: MAC Murder in Kfarze, Interview with Numan/47

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore xaṭər d- 'die Rücksicht auf j-n fahren lassen'

data.headword: ṭrele/ṭore xaṭər d- 'die Rücksicht auf j-n fahren lassen'
data.turoyo: e, ṭray u xaṭər diḏi w b ḥəsn w rəḏ̣a w isaniye kubaʕno menux. W kəbʕət b šarṭ, mu sayfo ste am marǧaʕ kili qumux no.
data.translation: eh, so laß lieber die Rücksicht auf mich (und meine Krankheit) fahren und ich will dich gütlich bitten. Wenn du aber die Bedingung des Schwertes willst, so stehe ich dir wiederum zur Verfügung.

rationale: Xaṭər lookup finds other light-verb phrases but none with ṭry. Abstract-noun collocation, one source; no numbered sense.

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore (mit ʕal aloho) 'etwas Gott überlassen'

data.turoyo: Ṭraya ʕal aloho!
data.translation: Überlaß das Gott!

rationale: Divine ʕal-goal and anaphoric object support an entrusting phrase; no ṭraya lookup match. One attestation, existing I.2.

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore i masale bayn X w Y 'eine Sache unter sich behalten'

data.headword: ṭrele/ṭore i masale bayn X w Y 'eine Sache unter sich behalten'
data.turoyo: Nošo lo koḏəʕ. W ṭraya i masale bayn eli w elax!
data.translation: Niemand weiß etwas; und du laß die Sache zwischen mir und dir bleiben!

rationale: Secrecy explicitly supplies the confidentiality reading. Masale search finds no matching ṭry collocation; one source.

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore X amane gab Y 'j-n/etwas j-m als anvertrautes Gut überlassen'

data.headword: ṭrele/ṭore X amane gab Y 'j-n/etwas j-m als anvertrautes Gut überlassen'
data.turoyo: Omər: “U=ḥaǧǧiyano azze l u=ḥaǧ w ṭrele i=barṯayḏe amane gab u=faqqayḏe.”
data.translation: Es fuhr fort: "Dieser Mekkapilger ging auf die Wallfahrt und vertraute seine Tochter seinem Schulmeister an."

rationale: Amane gives entrusted status; gab gives custodian. Lookup finds only other roots; light-verb phrase under I.2.

summary: New idiom: ṭrowe/ṭrowat xaṭər d- 'j-n/eine Sache um ... willen schonen, durchgehen lassen'

data.headword: ṭrowe/ṭrowat xaṭər d- 'j-n/eine Sache um ... willen schonen, durchgehen lassen'
data.turoyo: Ṭrowe xaṭər daʕ ʕayne kome!
data.translation: Laß ihn den schwarzen Augen Geschenkt sein!

rationale: The explicit stay-of-execution context at 105/73 and /136 fixes the sparing use; 95/261–262 show for-someone’s-sake preservation too. Distinct from ṭray xaṭər d- abandon consideration (30/122). Xaṭər lookup in batch 2 found no matching ṭry phrase.

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore taṯir (mit ʕal; b-) 'eine Wirkung auf ... hinterlassen'

data.headword: ṭrele/ṭore taṯir (mit ʕal; b-) 'eine Wirkung auf ... hinterlassen'
data.turoyo: Ǧan: Qariwi Brahim bu mawtayḏe ṭrele taṯir rabo ʕal Məḏyaḏ lo?
data.translation: Jan: My qariv Brahim, through his death, left a great impact on Midyat, didn’t he?

rationale: Repeated taṯir object with ʕal/b targets; glossary taṯir search finds only an unrelated poison effect, and round 1 has no such collocation. Supplied project machine translation [MT].

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore X b qḏole d- 'j-m die Verantwortung für etwas überlassen'

data.headword: ṭrele/ṭore X b qḏole d- 'j-m die Verantwortung für etwas überlassen'
data.turoyo: Kiban ṭurenale b qḏole dann alman, da swediye w dann əngiliz...?
data.translation: Can we leave it hanging round the necks of the Germans, the Swedes and the English...?

rationale: Single clear language-responsibility context. qḏole lookup has no corresponding ṭry phrase. Supplied project machine translation [MT].

summary: New idiom: ṭrele/ṭore (mit ʕal i raġlo) 'j-n auf den Beinen halten, stützen (fig.)'

data.headword: ṭrele/ṭore (mit ʕal i raġlo) 'j-n auf den Beinen halten, stützen (fig.)'
data.turoyo: Yaʕni maṯlo, d ḏkərləx, mən yo d ṭrəlelox ʕal i raġlo? Əno d ləwewoli hawxa haymonuṯo, lə kmətyaqanno d qudarnowo manfaqno tre kṯowe!..
data.translation: That is, for example, what you mentioned, what kept you on your feet? If I had not had such faith, I do not believe I would have been able to bring out two books!..

rationale: A single clear work-and-faith context supports figurative sustaining. raġlo lookup has no corresponding phrase; do not add the uncertain li raġlo variant. Supplied project machine translation [MT].

summary: Original sense numbering is preserved. Modal ṭr-owe and ṭro plus a dependent verb were inconsistently filed under I.5; seven identifiable existing Imperativ examples are moved to I.1 without changing their wording. This raises modal coverage and prevents false thin-cell additions.

Clarified I.6 denotes direct-object non-interference; men-targets remain I.5, while object-plus-state frames remain I.2. The original hungry example is explicitly moved to I.2. The relation between modal ellipsis and retention still needs context-by-context assessment.
JL 15.6/8, JTM 1.6/7 and MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/110 support one 1b retaliation/tolerance construction with personal l-suffix. They do not establish separate verbs for forgive and punish.
Ṭre- with -wo and an L-agent supports a Preterit-wa box (Bilgic /6; Farida /83). Infectum-wa occurs both habitually and counterfactually. Bounded time adverbials alone do not change a box.

Short ṭər/ṭr and fused ṭrowe/Ṭrawyo show modal reduction; source t, r-loss and dense suffix sequences are not silently repaired. Ṭro in ṭrowelux haž me ruḥux scopes the following hwy clause; me ruḥux does not by itself make this I.4.

Lookup checks: graw yielded no hit, but gəraw finds the existing pledge example at prs 29/16. That phrase is already represented, so no duplicate pledge addition. ḥəsbe has no hit; raḥa and rišayxu show other roots but no matching ṭry collocations; haž likewise has no matching care idiom.

Reader claims that Infectum-wa contains an example consisting only of 6) are not borne out by the supplied parsed entry: 6) is an inherited stem note. The box has three actual sense-2 examples. No phantom example is deleted.

EL 81 and Hors 1/82 can be different page/verse systems for the same wording; supplied evidence does not authorize replacing the older citation. Context proposals crossing beyond the supplied verse (JL 17.5/14; PrS 36/31 and /73) are not quoted.

Routine counts corroborate frequency but preserve the readers’ original sense coding, including modal forms under 5. They cannot be treated as already corrected or added to this batch’s reviewed-token count.
All batch-1 deltas are retained. Transparent modal/assent forms filed by readers under I.5 are consistently reassigned to I.1; ordinary repetition does not justify thin-cell additions.

Earlier phrase description revised: the rišayxu basimo formula is a closing wish at 63/348 as well as a condolence at JTM 1.2/12. The cumulative headword now records the broader use; its original example remains.
Resulting-state and privative constructions remain I.2, including captivity, shame, lack of women/housekeeper and dead victims. Direct non-interference remains I.6.
Direct narrative topics occur at 11/42, 11/63 and 61/133; men-topics recur throughout 88. This is a participant/discourse extension, not a distinct narrative-transition sense.
At 87/144 the alignment flag is honoured: no translation is quoted. Its named attribution and extra reply are absent from the supplied Turoyo.
The 78/77 əšmo reputation/surpassing proposal is withheld because name/standing versus small-quantity reading is unresolved in Turoyo; German Namen cannot settle it.
No phantom example consisting of 6) is removed; as verified in batch 1 it is an inherited note, not an example. Source-crossing proposed cuts at PrS 74/87 and 53/79 are not used.
This artifact pass was rerun after validation caught an unresolved new-sense label for the amane occurrence. It was assigned to I.2 before any files were published.

Batch 3 retains the cumulative 1b subsense, numbering, all earlier corrections, examples and idioms. Custody amane gab at 88/243 repeats the collocation accepted from 88/240; it is not a second sense or example.

No Part. Pass. or Detransitive sense is introduced from 108/8. Ṭruyo elux is ambiguous with fused permissive ṭr+uyo, already seen in allocation constructions (25/65, Farida /94). The reader’s participial analysis cannot independently establish a new box.

Xaṭər d- in fused ṭrowe/ṭrowat expressions motivates sparing someone; the following conditional execution threats support this interpretation from Turoyo context. It is not the semantically opposite bare ṭray u xaṭər diḏi leave consideration aside.

At 98/49, the alignment flag states that Ṭrowe is absent from the German translation. No translation is quoted and no example is added; the flag’s throw/put paraphrase is also not accepted as a new lexical meaning.
Holding a chess piece b iḏe at 104/19 corroborates retention under I.2. It does not overturn the earlier merger of thumb-positioning into I.2.

Routine counts remain aggregate reader coding, not newly reviewed tokens. Across the three batches 333 supplied full records now have individual decisions, with duplicate words/tokens in a verse kept in their input order.

Round 2 only. Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is project machine translation [MT]; readings rest on the supplied Turoyo. Existing and round-1 wording and numbering are retained. No edition translation is inferred.
The Infinitiv ṭroyo d lebo fills a genuinely absent box; routine Imperativ and Infectum counts in the readers’ observations are stale because they omit round 1.

Register is mixed: conversational interviews include Turkish administrative institutions, publication work and the borrowed abstract taṯir, while preservation and condolence formulas continue spoken uses. These are not all instances of a learned written register.

The mouth-key image at Jan 3.56/1664 is recorded for inquiry only. Its negation could concern being unable to stop people speaking rather than depriving them of speech; the reader’s freedom-of-speech gloss is not established.
The alleged Infectum-wa example consisting only of 6) at Jan 3.28/704 was already checked in round 1: it is a stem note, not a phantom example to delete. No repeated entry correction is emitted.
Lookup searches for taṯir, qḏole, raġlo, maftaḥ and əšmo rabo were inspected before selecting new phrases. No matching ṭry phrase was found; no internet or other run was consulted.
JL 15.6/8 and JTM 1.6/7: is the let-off threat conventional with a personal l-suffix, or recoverable modal ellipsis? Proposed 1b is constructional and can be merged if speakers do not distinguish it.
JTM 3.3/11: why does positive kṭuryo d howe receive a negative prevention translation? Check polarity, rhetorical scope or omitted wording before publication as an example.
Hors 1/32: confirm segmentation of ṭrallalli. JL 17.6/12: resolve masculine -lux in the exchange with the wife. PrS 35/58: verify r-less Ṭəyulle, which is not separately translated.
Lahdo Traitor 2/74–75: does bu ṣənəf imply repeating a completed grade, or merely being kept in the class? No technical numbered sense is introduced on translation alone.
PrS 18/74: is Trowe a leave form with an object ending, or fused ṭro+owe? Sense assignment is withheld.
MAC blessings: distinguish preserve/spare, permit one’s share and forgive; no supplied edition translation is silently replaced. What does dəṯxu resume at NE Interview 2/49?
Lahdo The snake/8: can the abandoned ṭralle clause be recovered? JTM 2.2/2: is -la the pepper as beneficiary or retained material as patient?
MAC Numan/47: confirm whether care for oneself is fixed as the whole ṭro+owe-lux haž phrase. The collocation is supported by one source only.
87/144: verify the German attribution and audience reply; current alignment warning prevents quotation.
PrS 37/75: resolve final -la in ṭəryola for a male actor. PrS 59/70: segment ṭrelelayo. 74/97: resolve lo ... lo polarity before treating leave-alone as positive.
53/149: ṭry with a dependent result clause or formally overlapping ṭyr? 81/103: identify Hano and the omitted argument before choosing a sense.
78/77: is əšmo name/reputation or a small-quantity word? No specific reputation idiom is published.
Confirm fused ṭruyo (25/65), ṭrowutu (61/375), ṭroweno (64/89), and final r in ṭrower (67/112).
Are xaṭər d-, ʕal aloho and masale bayn X w Y fixed with ṭry? Each rests on one source. Does the closing wish differ prosodically from condolence?
108/8: is ṭruyo a Part. Pass. form or fused ṭr+uyo in the allocation predicate? The proposed Detransitive box is withheld pending confirmation.
98/49: restore or identify the missing edition translation of Ṭrowe; do not quote the current aligned portion for that command.
96/202 and the SAY/LEAVE refrain 114/6, /14: does ṭry specifically mean leave unsaid or broadly leave/retain? Existing I.2 is retained.
93/31: is -la the colony/honey or the preceding story? Both permit existing I.2, so no narrative-specific sense is needed.
Confirm segmentation of gṭəryalliyo (97/132), expanded ṭrelelelan (112/173), and ṭrowat; keep exact written forms pending confirmation.
115/294: does bi dukṯo conventionally imply death with ṭry independently of a lethal context? Current evidence does not establish a kill-instantly idiom.
Explain ṭrele mayo at Jan 2.2/83, ṭrele lu Sayfo at Jan 3.1/17 and kṭəryo at Jan 4.I/550 before assigning a precise sense.
Resolve lo ṭray at Jan 1.8/213, ṭər ubelan at /1466, Lə ṭreli d umarli at /2123, and the scope of lə ṭralle at /2591. Positive machine paraphrases do not settle their polarity or omitted arguments.
At Jan 2.4/872, is Alo ṭrelox a reduced Infectum blessing or a Preterit? The transparent ṭurelox examples are Infectum; no new Preterit blessing example is published.
Confirm the three singly attested new phrases: responsibility b qḏole d-, sustaining ʕal i raġlo, and the independent li raġlo wording at Jan 4.I/229. The last is withheld.
What does negated ṭry maftaḥ d femo at Jan 3.56/1664 mean, and who can or cannot speak?
Confirm the contraction in ṭranne, written ṭrewayli, and final ṭruyo in the disjunctive series. No Detransitive or Part. Pass. box follows from the latter.
Jan 2.31/5177: does ṭrele i nuro release the fire or leave it unused? Jan 2.35/5620: what object is omitted? Jan 3.21/495 and 3.56/1692: resolve the elliptical modal clauses.
Jan examples have project machine translations [MT], not edition translations. Editors should check these English renderings against the Turoyo before treating them as vetted translations.
Correct the plural after 'one of her'
rationale: The count noun after 'one of her' must be plural. The supplied JL 13.11/10 translation has 'eines von ihren Küken'.

summary: Object plus resulting state already belongs here: waiting for hours, thumb kept hawxa, roofs left as earth, a person left alive or without blows. These do not mean leaving in peace.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/48
MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/23

summary: Retention includes a calculated manufacturing allowance (ḥəsbe/ter), food storage and breeding stock; no separate senses for materials or animals.
Keeping a pupil bu ṣənəf is an educational application of retention; three tokens belong to one episode. A conventional repeat-a-school-year meaning remains unproven.
Men-governed abandonment ranges over pursued individuals, religious allegiance, army/family ties and a topic left aside in narration.
Narratorial leaving of topics or characters at a scene specialises leave/retain; direct topics remain I.2 and men-topics I.5.
Ships leaving a wake and visits left fruitless extend participants to inanimate cause and abstract patient, without new senses.
Dependent sight and water-pouring events can carry enabling/coercive force; keep the shared lassen construction.
Divine preservation formula protects a young animal as well as people.
Measured material remainder (a horn left about fifteen centimetres) is ordinary retention with a measurement predicate, not a new technical sense.
Affliction retained in one’s heart and what is left unspoken in a SAY/LEAVE refrain are abstract-patient extensions; speech omission is not independently lexicalised.
Leaving someone bi dukṯo can be interpreted as leaving a corpse after killing or a deadly sting; the place phrase does not itself encode instantaneous death.
Men-marked narrative topic shift continues the earlier discourse extension.

Jan repeatedly supports the round-1 preservation gloss: God is the expressed subject, with a personal suffix or possessive object. The frequent conversational formula need not be reintroduced as a sense.
Repeated cause/motive questions use ṭry plus a d-clause; this supports the causal force already retained in round 1, rather than a new prompt verb.
Reduced ṭər/ṭr, fused ṭrowe assent, and disjunctive be-it enumeration recur. Assent is not newly filed under I.5; the round-1 moves are retained.
Administrative aid assigned to Kızılay and possessions left to a recipient extend the recipient and theme classes of leave/retain.
Retaining a guest with a duration/location is ordinary I.2; the l-marked nominal bishop accompanies the suffixed agent at /2405–2406.
Spatial m- departure is covered by verlassen; do not collapse it into men-governed non-interference merely because the same preposition occurs.
Abstract products include effects, a great name/reputation and a resulting commotion; these do not establish separate senses for every result noun.
Kṭəryolan occurs twice with feminine ʕade and result-location phrases; comparison with kṭəryo supports Infectum rather than the reader’s Preterit or conjectural ko-Preterit.
